title: In vitro antimicrobial activity of Cinnamomum verum, Allium sativum, and Zingiber officinale extracts
author: Yousefi Nojookambari, N.
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0

steps.title: Assess antibiotic resistance
steps.instruction: Evaluate the antibiotic resistance pattern of MBL-producing P. aeruginosa isolates using the Kirby‑Bauer disk diffusion method.

steps.title: Perform combined disk test
steps.instruction: Phenotypically test the isolates for metallo‑β‑lactamase production by the combined disk test (CDT).

steps.title: Detect MBL genes by PCR
steps.instruction: Detect the presence of blaVIM and blaIMP genes in the isolates using polymerase chain reaction (PCR).

steps.title: Determine MIC of plant extracts
steps.instruction: Determine the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of acetonic, methanolic, and chloroformic extracts of cinnamon, garlic, and ginger on MBL‑producing isolates by the broth microdilution method.

steps.title: Record MBL prevalence
steps.instruction: Document that 81 of 95 (85.2%) imipenem‑resistant P. aeruginosa isolates were MBL‑producing.

steps.title: Record gene frequencies
steps.instruction: Document that 13 of 81 (16.0%) isolates were blaIMP‑positive and 18 of 81 (22.2%) were blaVIM‑positive.

steps.title: Note extract inhibitory ranges
steps.instruction: Note that inhibitory concentrations of the acetonic, methanolic, and chloroformic extracts of cinnamon, garlic, and ginger ranged from ≥1.50 mg/ml to ≥12.50 mg/ml; the methanolic extracts of cinnamon and garlic and the acetonic extract of ginger showed significant antibacterial activity.
